cases.reason: Rule 3b is word-identical, but in 2002 a free-form line may be a DEBUGGING line (floating indicator >>D, §2002:6.1.2; §2002:6.3.4), a line kind 2023 does not have (its fixed and floating indicator tables list no debugging indicator, §2023:6.2.2, §2023:6.2.3.1). Rule 3b asks whether control characters may be specified in comments and literals; in 2002 a debugging line without WITH DEBUGGING MODE has the characteristics of a comment line, and 2002's free-form comments clause points at rule 3b explicitly, so the determination (LF only; a lone CR is a character of a comment or a literal) reaches the text of a >>D line in both modes. The 2023 row's witness (pb1496_lone_cr_is_a_character) has no debugging line, and the reader's evidence for it was a code read. Same cause as the reader's own DIFFERENT for item 125. Probes at --std 2002 (correct): dcr_nodebug.cob, '>>D DISPLAY "HIDDEN"<CR>DISPLAY "LEAK-AFTER-CR".' without debugging mode prints only END (the lone CR does not end the comment-like line); dcr_debug.cob, '>>D DISPLAY "LEN=" FUNCTION LENGTH("A<CR>B")' with debugging mode prints LEN=3. Both are COBOL0902 at --std 2023.
